openwrt_commit.commit_nachricht:
From 19d770d7b91aaca1de18281dea0da8616df34c6c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pawel Dembicki <paweldembicki@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Aug 2024 22:47:47 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] mediatek: filogic: add support for Cudy AP3000 Outdoor

Hardware highlights:
  - MediaTek MT7981 WiSoC
  - 256MB DDR3 RAM
  - 64MB SPI-NAND
  - MediaTek MT7981 2x2 DBDC 802.11ax 2T2R (2.4 / 5)
  - 1x LED in two colors
  - 2x Button
  - 1x 1GbE
  - Two detachable antenas, two internal pcb antenas
  - PoE powered (standalone)

MAC:
LAN MAC: label mac
2.4G MAC: label mac -1
5G MAC: label mac

How to install:
1. Apply Cudy Intermediate OpenWrt image for AP3000 Outdoor V1
2. Install OpenWrt sysupgrade image

Signed-off-by: Pawel Dembicki <paweldembicki@gmail.com>
Link: https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/pull/16156
Signed-off-by: Hauke Mehrtens <hauke@hauke-m.de>

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rgSdzU7vCZd1TM2wJiGPx2qXGQnu_HJV/view?usp=drivesdk
I just ordered a pair of this device and will be able to test in a few days. Thanks a lot for your work!

@obsy  from  eko.one.pl (polish unofficial support site) released 23.05 images for this AP:
https://dl.eko.one.pl/firmware/?version=luci-23.05-SNAPSHOT&target=mediatek%2Ffilogic&id=cudy_ap3000outdoor-v1#
Why do we need a binary "intermediate" image, and why was building this intermediate image not included in OpenWrt? This feels extremely dodgy.

> @stintel
> 
> > Why do we need a binary "intermediate" image, and why was building this intermediate image not included in OpenWrt? This feels extremely dodgy.
> 
> OFW accept only signed images. You need "intermediate" image signed by Cudy, which doesn't check if sysupgrade images are signed. Every Cudy devices have the same issue. But outdoor AP are glued and you can't access serial without destroying device. Imtermediate image is the only way.

Thanks for the explanation. I would like to revert the commit, and reapply it with this extra info in the commit message. I probably should have done more research, but if I'd known about this intermediate image, I'd probably not have bought this device.
Maybe good wiki article could be enough?

> 
> I have several AP3000 Outdoor which are not glued, only the screws need to be removed

Did you extract pcb? In my device pcb are glued inside case. I can remove two screws, but I can't extract board.
There's a ring screw nut outside on each RP-SMA socket, under a little plastic sticker ring. Remove that in addition to the case screws, and the board slides out
Hmmm, my board have RP-SMA on cables with pigtails.

Hi Developer,
I am Sam, the Technical support engineer of Cudy. We have changed the model of the Flash (ROM) ESMT F50L1G41LC in the Cudy AP3000 Outdoor recently. The current OpenWrt firmware will not work on the AP3000 Outdoor V1.0 now. To fix this issue, we have made a new patch to add the support for the new flash and still work with old Flash. Please have a check and merge it.
[999-mtd-spinand-esmt-Add-support-for-F50L1G41LC.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23468636/999-mtd-spinand-esmt-Add-support-for-F50L1G41LC.patch)
Note: this patch based on Linux kernel 5.15.158.

Here is the same link for Cudy TR3000 V1.0. Please check.
https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/pull/20805

Thank you @Samxieerbao , fixed in 9424b2b78626702012dc73616bfd21029712b5f7 and c84025dea29602d149d22a86502d784f292441fe and backported to 24.10 in 6ff763e78ceff83ffef7db08f7cc364bbc05ca50 and 804a2e6c513187cb809dfc890f2660fac1b3fd99

I just received this device and installed the intermediate image mentioned at the [top](https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt/pull/16156#issuecomment-2289409501) of this thread.
It failed to boot afterwards (constant red light and no wifi active).
I possibly could have reached it via cable, but I guess I was discouraged by the red light.
However, with the information in this thread I was able to open it and connect via serial.
The linked image from above is an openwrt 2023.05 image, and even though the LED was red, access was available via serial. I was able to modify the network config, reboot, scp the image on the device, and sysupgrade -n.

produkt_json.body_html: A pole/wall-mounted WiFi 6 AP featuring eFEM providing exceptional range performance. The IP65 casing, PoE, and Cudy Mesh features, ideal for high-density park, farm, and parking lot environments.

Hardware Specs.Range Performance: Max: 320 m (1050 ft); Park: 280 m (919 ft); Street: 70 m (230 ft); Woods: 40 m (131 ft)
Hardware Specs.EMC: IEC/EN 61000-4-2, Level 3 ESD: Contact: 6kV; Air: 8kV; IEC/EN 61000-4-5, Level 4 Surge: Power: DM 2kV, CM 4kV; RJ45: CM 4kV

Hardware Specs.Ingress Protection Rating: IP65 When devices is installed vertically
Hardware Specs.Package Content: AP3000 Outdoor; Detachable Antennas; PoE Adapter; Power Cord; Mounting Kit; Ethernet Cable; Installation Guide

Software Specs.Multi-SSID (Max Number): 8 SSIDs (Up to 4 SSIDs on each band), VLAN Support
Software Specs.Operation Modes: Wi-Fi Router; Access Point; Range Extender; WISP; Client
Software Specs.Mesh Backhaul: Wireless Backhaul; Wired Backhaul; Multi-Band Backhaul
Software Specs.WAN Mode: DHCP; Static IP; PPPOE; PPTP; L2TP
Software Specs.IPv6 Protocols: Relay; Dynamic (SLAAC/DHCPv6); Static (Fixed IP); Passthrough; 464XLAT; MAP-E; DS-Lite

Kurzinfo.Sonstiges: Multi-AP Management; Watchdog, Schedule Reboot; Max 320 m (1050 ft) Range; 200 Connected Devices

Werbetext.High-Power Wi-Fi Coverage with Five PA: Equipped with five power amplifiers and a 3+2 antenna structure, this AP delivers top-notch capabilities to navigate its signal through physical obstacles.
Werbetext.Works in Rain, Thunder, Dust, Heat, Cold: The AP is protected by an IP65 standard case, shielding it from rain and dust when installed vertically. It also features 6 kV Lightning/Surge and 8 kV ESD protection for higher reliability in thunderstorms. Its working temperatures span from -40 °F to 158 °F (-40 ℃ to 70 ℃).
Werbetext.Gigabit Port with Two PoE Options: Supports two powering methods— 802.3at PoE (Max power: 18 W, Idle: 5 W); 48-57 V Passive PoE (Adapter included, not waterproof)
Werbetext.Mounting Kit Included: A mounting kit is included in the box, supporting— Wall-Mounting; Pole-Mounting
Werbetext.Centralized AP Management: Easily manage up to 200 access points with Cudy AP Controller (Model:C200P)

1. Support Parental Control. 2. Fix some bugs.

1. Add APP support. 2. Add online Upgrade and Auto Upgrade. 3. Adjusted the administrator password mechanism in accordance with the requirements of ETSI EN 303 645. 4. Add WiFi isolation support. 5. Add Client mode. 6. Fix some bugs.

openwrt_pr_24567.text_flash: Both boards are fitted with an ESMT F50L2G41XA SPI-NAND (256 MiB), but the existing device trees only expose a 64 MiB `ubi` partition, leaving ~186 MiB of flash unused.
openwrt_pr_24567.text_varianz: Field units may vary in flash size (as has happened on other boards in this family)
openwrt_pr_24567.text_layout: 256mb-v1 variant with a full-size ubi partition (0x5c0000-0x10000000), only installable via TFTP/recovery
openwrt_pr_24567.text_test: Not tested on real hardware -- I don't own either board.

kommentare.text: The originals  are kind of 128MB with great slack space too.... You have to, OEM bootloader may disagree with new partition scheme....
this board doesn't have a custom OpenWrt u-boot (no patch under package/boot/uboot-mediatek/) ... Parking this PR until someone with the hardware can confirm one way or the other.
Agree. I already tried expanding the partition on Cudy, but it bricked the device because the stock bootloader wouldn't work with a partition of a different size.
Closing this, the approach isn't safe as-is on stock bootloader.
(ohne Sachinhalt)

lauf.notiz: Neu: Cudy-FAQ belegt Flash-Wechsel ab Seriennummer 2543 (KW 43/2025) auch fuer AP3000 Outdoor 1.0, Downgrade-Sperre <=2.3.X, OpenWrt >=24.10.5; Intermediate 20251119 im ffnef-Spiegel. Gluon-PR 3384: nur Web-UI, kein TFTP, Reset->Config Mode, is_outdoor_device. PR 24567/Issue 24565 behaupten 256 MiB F50L2G41XA (unbelegt, Log vom Innen-AP3000). FCC: auch per Volltextsuche keine ID. Seriell-Pinbelegung, Luefter, Heizung unter OpenWrt weiter offen. Blockaden: www.reddit.com 403, api.github.com 403 (Rate-Limit).

lauf1.notiz: Nicht im ToH-Dump, Datenseite cudy_ap3000_outdoor_v1 vorhanden. Aussengeraet IP65, nur PoE (802.3at oder passiv 48-57 V, Netzteil liegt bei). Widersprueche: Flash 128 (Hersteller/ToH/WikiDevi) vs 64 MB (Commit, OpenWrt nutzt 64 MiB), 5-GHz-Ketten 3T3R/2T3R/2T2R, Funkchip MT7976CN vs DAN, Temperaturbereich (65/70/60 °C), Antennen intern 1 vs 2. Ab Ende 2025 Flash ESMT F50L1G41LC: braucht OpenWrt >= 24.10.5 (in Gluon v2025.1.3 enthalten). Keine FCC-ID, seriell Pinbelegung offen, DeviWiki ohne Eintrag, Forum 429.

geizhals.ergebnis: heise-Suche 1 Treffer a3652198 (Cudy AP3000 Outdoor, AX3000) + Produktseite (2 heise-Abrufe); Modell hat nur Hardware-Version V1.0; Datenblatt (24 Zeilen) nach roh.geizhals, Felder ergaenzt; keine EAN/ASIN auf der Seite

entschieden: flash_mb: 128 MB gilt (Hersteller-Datenblatt V1.0, Produktseite, neuer Flash F50L1G41LC = 1 Gbit); 64 widerlegt (nur ubi-Partition, DTS-Layout reicht bis ca. 69,75 MiB); 256 widerlegt (Bootlog vom Innen-AP3000 v1, PR 24567 ungetestet und ungemergt)
